metadata.file_name: 91. Pejic et al. (2021). Math proficiency prediction in computer-based international large-scale assessments using a multi-class machine learning model.pdf
metadata.title: Math proficiency prediction in computer-based international large-scale assessments using a multi-class machine learning model
metadata.venue: IEEE 19th International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY)

design_fields.q1_rationale: Matching IEEE full-text PDF states that the outcome is student proficiency classes engineered from PISA 2012 CBA cognitive item responses rather than PISA population plausible values; no multiple-PV combination is used.
design_fields.q2_rationale: Matching IEEE full-text PDF does not report applying PISA student sampling weights. No explicit unweighted-analysis statement was found.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The full-text methods describe student-level neural-network/random-forest models and a random 70:30 record-level train/test split, without a school-level split or multilevel/cluster-robust adjustment.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The PDF reports an internal 70:30 train/test split plus neural-network validation within the training portion, with no external cycle/country/dataset transfer.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 91. Pejic et al. (2021). Math proficiency prediction in computer-based international large-scale assessments using a multi-class machine learning model.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: The paper explicitly processes the whole multi-country PISA 2012 CBA dataset (271,323 student records) in pooled models rather than country-specific models.
